focus: Build the three deliverables from the four inventories: the removal order with a gate after each step, the user-machine cleanup design (vector tables, backup copies, model server, HuggingFace cache, pulled Ollama model, env keys, build output) and the residue check with repo and machine modes; settle the carried-forward open checks and state the operator decisions as options
noveltyJustification: 8 of 14 findings are fully new (gates, plain-table schema, machine observation, dotenv guard, external delete APIs, residue baseline, closed checks, routing-neutrality gate) and 6 are built mostly from earlier inventories with new evidence added.
keyQuestions: What removal order keeps every gate green, how are repo users machines cleaned (pulled model, vector tables, background server, env vars) without a backup, and what residue check proves nothing is left?
answeredQuestions: What removal order keeps every gate green, how are repo users machines cleaned (pulled model, vector tables, background server, env vars) without a backup, and what residue check proves nothing is left?
ruledOut: Routing the database cleanup through /doctor:skill-advisor rebuild: it backs the old database up and keeps the copy, which carries the vectors forward.
A build-tool clean for the shared package's stale output: it works from sources that still exist, and the package has no clean script.
Reading .env with a shell command: a hook refuses it; the sanctioned route returns key names only.
Persisting a keep-the-model answer: it writes new lane state onto the user's machine.
Directory-prefix allowlist rows: they would hide a real remnant placed in those folders later; rows are exact paths.
sourcesQueried: this machine: ollama model store, process list, dist, node_modules, .env key names

label: The gates each removal step is checked against already exist: advisor typecheck, vitest and clean build; shared build and tests; the doctor run-all.sh; derive-command-bridges --check; generate-trigger-index --check (report-only in CI); the markdown link check; four CI routing ratchets; advisor stress and full suite in CI; generate-leaf-manifest --check. The global pre-commit hook runs mirror --check, leaf manifest --check, the doc version bump check and the parent-skill doctor on every commit.

Eight groups of edits cannot be split across commits: the lane id with every Record<ScorerLane, number> literal; the install route, checklist and contract test entry; doctor callers of the semantic-health flag with or before the strict schema key; the ablation test with holdout-independent.vitest.ts line 95 (CI runs that suite by name); scoring-compatibility.json before the bridge regeneration; a deleted routed doc with its leaf manifest (writer is generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --write); the shared embeddings folder with shared/types.ts line 5; the HuggingFace dependency with doctor.sh 58 and INSTALL-GUIDE.md 105.

Removal order in eight steps, each with a gate: 0 baseline plus the residue check in report-only mode (must exit 1 with 332 files) and the unwired cleanup tool; 1 doctor surface and bridge regeneration; 2 lane feeders (vector refresh, prompt embedding, exact rerank, command meaning path, embeddingText); 3 lane id, status contract, vector DDL, embedders folder and the dead env flag (compiler-forced atomic); 4 shared embeddings package, HF model server, launcher supervision, sk-doc validator and the npm dependency; 5 prose docs and identity files; 6 derived artifacts (trigger index, skill-graph export, cite-drift labels); 7 wire the cleanup into /doctor:update apply and flip the residue check to gating. The order was derived, not executed.

The vector tables are plain SQLite tables with a BLOB column in a database the rebuild workflow calls derived state; the driver is better-sqlite3 and no extension is loaded. Recommended cleanup of existing databases: raise SCHEMA_VERSION and add a generic rule that discards a database with an older stored version (main file, -wal, -shm) and rescans. The rule names no table, so it carries no lane vocabulary. Dropping in place keeps lane names in migration code and leaves dropped rows in free pages unless VACUUM runs. Two confirmations are open: automatic rescan of an empty database at daemon start, and the content of skill_graph_metadata.

Copies of the database carry the vectors: the rebuild workflow writes a .bak copy before rebuilding and keeps it on success, /doctor:update apply prompts for that rebuild as phase 6, and the database directory also holds runtime-quarantined .corrupt copies. The machine cleanup therefore runs after the update's rebuild prompt and deletes every .bak and .corrupt sibling by name pattern.

Observed on this machine, read-only: compiled lane output under the advisor dist/runtime/lib and under shared/dist/embeddings; @huggingface and onnxruntime-node installed in both packages; Ollama installed with nomic-embed-text v1.5 as the only library entry; no ollama or hf-model-server process running; no /tmp/system-hf-embed; .env holds 11 keys, none from the lane; seven runtime config files have zero matches.

A pre-tool hook refuses any shell read of a dotenv file and names env-secret.cjs keys, validate and fingerprint as the sanctioned route. The cleanup must detect stale lane keys through the keys mode and report them; no write mode was seen, and whether /doctor:env has a remove mode was not read.

External delete paths: Ollama removes a model with DELETE /api/delete and a required model field, answered 200, and its page does not say what happens to shared layers. The HuggingFace cache defaults to ~/.cache/huggingface/hub (moved by HF_HOME or HF_HUB_CACHE), stores a model in one models--org--name folder, is shared across libraries, and hf cache rm removes one repo with --dry-run and --yes.

User-machine cleanup design: one tool with report and apply modes, run per checkout and per linked worktree, deleting and never copying. Without asking: discard and rescan the database, delete .bak and .corrupt copies and vector shards, stop a model server whose command line is this checkout's script and delete /tmp/system-hf-embed, clean and rebuild advisor dist, delete shared/dist by path, npm ci. Ask first: the exact HuggingFace cache folder and the pulled Ollama model, because both stores are shared and nothing records the pull. Report only: a running ollama serve (pid never recorded) and lane env keys in dotenv files. SPEC_KIT_DB_DIR and the stores' own env keys are kept.

Residue baseline at commit 44251c5befd over tracked files with specs excluded: 279 files on the identifier pattern, 163 on the prose pattern, 332 in the union, 23 of them in changelog folders; 7,541 tracked files under specs match. One match under cli-classifier is in no earlier inventory and was not opened.

Residue check design, built as a sibling of sweep-memory-residue.mjs with its exit contract (0 clean, 1 live hits, 2 invocation error) and exemptions as data rows with reasons. Repo mode: both patterns over tracked files with specs excluded, tracked file names, generator check modes, a regenerate-then-assert rule for the trigger index, dependency rows, the symlink, behavioral probes (flag refused, four lane keys, no embeddings field, six doctor targets) and a planted-term fixture that must exit 1. Machine mode: build output, node_modules, every SQLite file including a byte search, processes, the HuggingFace folder, the Ollama model, dotenv key names and linked worktrees. The check, its allowlist and its test are the one permanent holder of the vocabulary.

Closed checks: the leaf manifest writer is generate-leaf-manifest.cjs; the RSS watchdog env subsection goes because only model-server-supervision.cjs uses those keys; SPEC_KIT_DB_DIR stays because the worktree script exports it and deep-loop tests set it; the skill-advisor menu items 6 and 7 become 5 and 6; SKILL_ADVISOR_DISABLE_BUILTIN_SEMANTIC still has no reader and five more writer sites; conflict-query-rerank and lane-weight-sweep are edits, not deletions; the spec-kit tests/embedders listing matches iteration 2; daemon-lease-contract.md 138 is an edit and auto-note.md 19 is not a remnant.

No tracked JSON or JSONL file under the advisor runtime contains the lane id, cosine evidence or meaningPassed, and the lane's live weight is 0, so the four CI routing ratchets should pass in steps 2 and 3 with their score baselines untouched. A ratchet that needs recapturing means the removal changed routing. Only the regime field at scorer-eval-baseline.json line 9 changes by design. The empty grep could also come from a pathspec fault, so this is likely, not certain.

Seven operator decisions with a recommended default each: exclude changelog folders from the check instead of rewriting 23 released files; leave the shadow weights at 0.95; rename the three five-lane files to a name without a count; keep the sweeper's ollama-preserve guard with an allowlist row; ask on each run before removing a pulled model nobody can attribute; delete shared/chunking.ts and shared/utils/retry.ts with the package; discard and rescan existing databases.
Every Record<ScorerLane, number> literal drops the lane key in the same commit as the registry row.
A commit that deletes or renames a routed doc regenerates that skill's leaf manifest, because the pre-commit hook checks it per commit.
The routing ratchets pass with score baselines untouched in the steps that remove the lane; a needed recapture is a finding.
The machine cleanup deletes and never copies, asks before touching a store shared with other tools, and never stops a process it cannot attribute.
